content: Certainly. 1. A cohort study published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2017 (Volume 65, Pages 235-243) examined specific outcomes related to infectious diseases. 2. Jongbloed K, Pearce ME, Pooyak S, Zamar D, Thomas V, Demerais L, and colleagues conducted a study titled The Cedar Project, which investigated mortality rates among young Indigenous individuals who use drugs in British Columbia. The findings were published in CMAJ in 2017 (Volume 189, Pages E1352-E1359). 3. Benova L, Mohamoud YA, Calvert C, and Abu-Raddad LJ performed a systematic review and meta-analysis on the vertical transmission of hepatitis C virus (HCV). Their work was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2014 (Volume 59, Pages 765-773). 4. Jafari S, Copes R, Baharlou S, Etminan M, and Buxton J conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the risk of hepatitis C transmission associated with tattooing. This study appeared in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2010 (Volume 14, Pages e928-e940). 5. Coppola N, De Pascalis S, Onorato L, Calò F, Sagnelli C, and Sagnelli E explored the prevalence and risks of hepatitis B and C virus infections among healthcare workers. Their findings were published in the World Journal of Hepatology in 2016 (Volume 8, Pages 273-281). 6. Westermann C, Peters C, Lisiak B, Lamberti M, and Nienhaus A conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the prevalence of hepatitis C among healthcare workers. This study was published in Occupational and Environmental Medicine in 2015 (Volume 72, Pages 880-888). 7. Danta M, Brown D, Bhagani S, Pybus OG, Sabin CA, Nelson M, and colleagues reported on an epidemic of acute hepatitis C virus infection among HIV-positive men who have sex with men, linked to high-risk sexual behaviors. This study was published in AIDS in 2007 (Volume 21, Pages 983-991). 8. Curry MP, O'Leary JG, Bzowej N, Muir AJ, Korenblat KM, Fenkel JM, and colleagues evaluated the efficacy of sofosbuvir and velpatasvir in patients with decompensated cirrhosis. Their findings were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2015 (Volume 373, Pages 2618-2628). 9. Feld JJ, Jacobson IM, Hézode C, Asselah T, Ruane PJ, Gruener N, and colleagues investigated the efficacy of sofosbuvir and velpatasvir for treating HCV genotypes 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6. This study was published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2015 (Volume 373, Pages 2599-2607). 10. Foster GR, Afdhal N, Roberts SK, Bräu N, Gane EJ, Pianko S, and colleagues examined the efficacy of sofosbuvir and velpatasvir in treating HCV genotypes 2 and 3. Their findings were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2015 (Volume 373, Pages 2608-2617). 11. Grebely J, Dore GJ, Zeuzem S, Aspinall RJ, Fox R, Han L, and colleagues analyzed the efficacy and safety of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir in patients with chronic HCV infection undergoing opioid substitution therapy. This analysis was part of the Phase 3 ASTRAL trials and was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2016 (Volume 63, Pages 1479-1481). 12. Wyles D, Bräu N, Kottilil S, Daar ES, Ruane P, Workowski K, and colleagues conducted an open-label Phase 3 study on the use of sofosbuvir and velpatasvir for treating HCV in patients co-infected with HIV-1. The study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2017 (Volume 65, Pages 6-12). 13. Kateera F, Shumbusho F, Manirambona L, Kabahizi J, Murangwa A, Serumondo J, and colleagues evaluated the safety and efficacy of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir in treatment-naïve patients with chronic HCV infection in Rwanda. This single-arm trial (SHARED-3) was published in The Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology in 2022. 14. Asselah T, Kowdley KV, Zadeikis N, Wang S, Hassanein T, Horsmans Y, and colleagues assessed the efficacy of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir for 8 or 12 weeks in patients with HCV genotypes 2, 4, 5, or 6 without cirrhosis. Their findings were published in Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology in 2018 (Volume 16, Pages 417-426). 15. Forns X, Lee SS, Valdes J, Lens S, Ghalib R, Aguilar H, and colleagues conducted a Phase 3 trial (EXPEDITION-1) on glecaprevir plus pibrentasvir for chronic HCV genotypes 1, 2, 4, 5, or 6 in adults with compensated cirrhosis. This study was published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2017 (Volume 17, Pages 1062-1068). 16. Gane E, Lawitz E, Pugatch D, Papatheodoridis G, Bräu N, Brown A, and colleagues evaluated glecaprevir and pibrentasvir in patients with HCV and severe renal impairment. Their findings were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2017 (Volume 377, Pages 1448-1455). 17. Gane E, Poordad F, Wang S, Asatryan A, Kwo PY, Lalezari J, and colleagues demonstrated the high efficacy of ABT-493 and ABT-530 in treating HCV genotypes 1 or 3 with compensated cirrhosis. This study was published in Gastroenterology. 18. Kwo PY, Poordad F, Asatryan A, Wang S, Wyles DL, Hassanein T, and colleagues reported high response rates with glecaprevir and pibrentasvir in patients with HCV genotypes 1-6 without cirrhosis. This study was published in Journal of Hepatology in 2017 (Volume 67, Pages 263-271). 19. Poordad F, Felizarta F, Asatryan A, Sulkowski MS, Reindollar RW, Landis CS, and colleagues evaluated glecaprevir and pibrentasvir for 12 weeks in patients with HCV genotype 1 and prior direct-acting antiviral treatment. Their findings were published in Hepatology in 2017 (Volume 66, Pages 389-397). 20. Rockstroh J, Lacombe K, Viani RM, Orkin C, Wyles D, Luetkemeyer A, and colleagues assessed the efficacy and safety of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir in patients co-infected with HCV and HIV-1 in the EXPEDITION-2 study. This abstract was presented at The International Liver Congress.
